biography.plain_text: Mariano Prado Sosa was a Peruvian banker and property developer from the family that controlled Banco Popular. Known as Marianito, he studied business administration at Stanford before taking a leading role in the family enterprise. The bank’s nationalisation ended that role; he subsequently pursued property and tourism projects in Spain and Peru.

long_biography.plain_text:
The Laguna Azul hotel made Mariano Prado Sosa an early promoter of tourism around Lake Sauce in Peru’s San Martín region. He opened the lakeside venture in 1982 and helped develop the local airfield, making the area more accessible to visitors. The lodge consisted of ten cabins. Political violence eventually forced him to abandon the project.

Property development had occupied Prado Sosa well before his Amazonian venture. In Lima he developed the Chama and Residencial Higuereta neighbourhoods and the Monterrico shopping centre. During his years in Spain, he directed the construction of hotels and housing developments outside Madrid, where he lived with his wife and children.
